limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that scripts/flow-ci-status.sh's FLOW_CI_FAILURE_ORIGIN classifies a failed commands-type step by its EXIT CODE (75, EX_TEMPFAIL - the convention ci-stage-jq.py/ci-stage-git.py/ci-stage-make.py all return for 'could not fetch'), not only by the provider's step TYPE (clone). The bad case (a jq-stage-shaped step failing with exit 75) must report precode; the good case (the same step failing with exit 1, the sha256/scheme-mismatch code) must still report code - the must-not-flip anchor, since laundering a tampered-bytes finding into precode would be worse than the defect #1411 fixes. The gate's OWN exit code does not vary with this distinction (it is 0 unless --exit-code is passed, and then 1 for any failure, precode or not), so run-case.sh does not pass it through: it reads FLOW_CI_FAILURE_ORIGIN from stdout and recomputes a verdict-shaped exit itself (0 for code, 1 for precode), which is what good_exit and detect_signal are read against. NO NETWORK, NO WOODPECKER SERVER: run-case.sh puts a stub curl first on PATH and answers the gate's three real calls (repo lookup, pipeline list, one pipeline's workflow detail) from fixed JSON, varying only the one failed step's exit_code per case - the same no-network shape controls/lane-serveability-check already uses for an HTTP-fetching gate. TRANSPORT IS NOT EXERCISED: this proves the CLASSIFICATION of a given exit code, not how Woodpecker's API actually renders one, and not the woodpecker-cli fallback lane (a separate code path this control does not reach - it has no verified way to carry a per-step exit code today, so it stays on the pre-#1411 behaviour by construction, not by a case here). Does not cover the clone-type half of FLOW_CI_FAILURE_ORIGIN (#1342's own prior control, if one exists, or the existing tests/test_flow_ci_status.py cases), the MIXED verdict, or a step with no exit_code field at all. MEASURED directly (issue #1411): the first draft of run-case.sh's embedded curl stub used bash's ${@: -1} to read the last argument, and /bin/sh here resolves to dash - a silent 'Bad substitution' on every stub invocation, which wp_api's own 2>/dev/null swallowed into an empty REPO_ID and read as 'no provider answered', not as a stub bug. Fixed with a POSIX-safe 'for url in "$@"; do :; done' loop; the case file below is what caught it, by failing to run at all rather than by scoring wrong.
